{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Daniel Ken Nakano''' (born July 30, 1964)<ref name="cv">[http://www.math.uga.edu/~nakano/vita.html Curriculum vitae] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100613152208/http://www.math.uga.edu/~nakano/vita.html |date=2010-06-13 }}, retrieved 2015-01-24.</ref> is an American mathematician. Nakano is a Distinguished Research Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of Georgia]]; he specializes in [[representation theory]].<ref name="5named">[http://www.math.uga.edu/FivefacultymembersnamedinauguralAMSFellows.htm Five faculty members named inaugural AMS Fellows] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150101071118/http://www.math.uga.edu/FivefacultymembersnamedinauguralAMSFellows.htm |date=2015-01-01 }}, U. Georgia Mathematics, retrieved 2015-01-24.</ref>

Nakano was born in [[Seattle]], Washington.<ref name="cv"/> His parents are [[Japanese Americans|Japanese American]], and he grew up in [[Kirkland, Washington]].<ref name=uga>{{cite web| title=Daniel Nakano| url=https://news.uga.edu/daniel-nakano/|publisher=University of Georgia |date=2019-04-07}}</ref> Nakano graduated from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1986,<ref name="cv"/> and earned a doctorate in mathematics from [[Yale University]] in 1990 under the supervision of [[George Seligman|George B. Seligman]] with thesis ''Projective Modules over Lie Algebras of Cartan Type''.<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=26482}}</ref> After temporary positions at [[Auburn University]] and [[Northwestern University]], he became an assistant professor at [[Utah State University]] in 1994 and moved to the University of Georgia in 2001.<ref name="cv"/>

In 2010, Nakano was named Distinguished Research Professor.<ref name="cv"/>
In 2012, he became one of the inaugural [[fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2015-01-24.</ref>

In 2016, he received the Lamar Dodd Award Creative Research Award.

==Publications==
*[http://bookstore.ams.org/pspum-92/ ''Lie Algebras, Lie Superalgebras, Vertex Algebras and Related Topics''], American Mathematical Society, (2016)
